column1: # POINTER-based BYTE reads of the LOW HALF of a 16-bit field (2026-08-02).
# line <tab> evidence
# Why a separate list from le_read_sites.tsv: there is nothing to byte-swap in
# a single byte. x86 puts a word's low half at offset +0, the 68k puts it at
# +1, so `mov al,[eax]` on a word field must become `move.b (1,a0),d0`. This
# list moves the DISPLACEMENT; le_read_sites.tsv swaps a VALUE. Mixing the two
# would be wrong in both directions.
# THE CASE THAT FOUND IT -- FUNC_001330_DPalBuild, which builds every palette
# entry the 3D view uses. It walks a colour-box record of six WORD bounds
# (min/max for R, G and B at a 4-byte stride) and takes the low byte of each:
#   mov eax,[esp+0x18] / mov al,[eax]      ; max R   (word at +0)
#   mov edx,[esp+0x18] / add al,[edx-0x2]  ; min R   (word at -2)
#   ... the same for G at +4/+2 and B at +8/+6
# The bounds hold 0..0x10, so their HIGH byte -- which is what the 68k read
# instead -- is ALWAYS ZERO. All three channels were therefore computed from
# zero, came out equal, and every palette entry was a pure grey. Measured on
# the running game: the 3D viewport used 10 distinct palette indices and every
# (60,60,60), (63,63,63) -- while the 2D console rendered in full colour.
# That is the whole reason the 3D view was black and white.

column2: FUNC_001330_DPalBuild: mov al,[eax] -- max R, low byte of the word at box+0
FUNC_001330_DPalBuild: add al,[edx-0x2] -- min R, low byte of the word at box-2
FUNC_001330_DPalBuild: mov al,[eax+0x4] -- max G, low byte of the word at box+4
FUNC_001330_DPalBuild: add al,[edx+0x2] -- min G, low byte of the word at box+2
FUNC_001330_DPalBuild: mov al,[eax+0x8] -- max B, low byte of the word at box+8
FUNC_001330_DPalBuild: add al,[edx+0x6] -- min B, low byte of the word at box+6

column1: # SUB-WORD ACCESSES INTO A DWORD FIELD (2026-08-03). Column 2 is the explicit
# displacement delta; rows without one still mean +1.
# THE CASE THAT FOUND IT -- FUNC_000832 packs the player's system id into the
# single dword field [DATA_008804+0x27c] using three different widths
#   x     = [ebx+0x25c] sar 16, & 0x1fff   -> mov [ebx+0x27c],ax   WORD, low half
#   y     = [ebx+0x260] sar 16, & 0x1fff   -> or'd in as a DWORD
#   index = arg1 & 0x3f, << 2              -> mov [ebx+0x27f],al   BYTE 3
# and the id is consumed as one packed integer by FUNC_000852 (x = bits 0..12,
# Untouched, the 68k put x in the HIGH half, where the very next instruction's
# `and edx,0xfc001fff` erased it, and put the index in the LOW byte instead of
# the top one. PREDICTED 0x00064000, and the running game MEASURED 0x00064000
# against the reference's 0x1aa51717 -- the whole system id, and so the entire
# star system, was wrong because of these four instructions.

column3: FUNC_000832: mov dx,[ebx+0x27c] -- word read of the LOW half of the id dword
FUNC_000832: mov [ebx+0x27c],ax -- word store into the LOW half of the id dword
FUNC_000832: mov dl,[ebx+0x27f] -- byte 3 (the TOP byte) of the id dword
FUNC_000832: mov [ebx+0x27f],al -- byte 3 (the TOP byte) of the id dword

column1: # THE PACKED FLOAT'S EXPONENT, INSIDE A RUN-TIME RECORD (2026-08-05).
# The star-system generator stores a packed float as ONE DWORD in each 0x44-byte
# body record and then bumps its EXPONENT with a 16-bit add at +2:
#     mov  [ebx+edi*4+0xe],eax                 ; the packed float, a dword
#     add  word [ebx+edi*4+0x10],byte +0x19    ; +25 to its exponent
# On x86 the high half of a dword at +0xe is at +0x10; on a 68k it is at +0xe,
# so the unshifted displacement adds 25 to the MANTISSA. frame.py already makes
# exactly this correction for the same idiom on the STACK (`add word
# [ebp-0x12],byte +0x32' over the dword at [ebp-0x14], ffe.asm:65325), but a
# field of a run-time record is neither a stack slot nor a named label, so
# nothing types it and the site table has to.
# Evidence, pooled over the whole generator family (ffe.asm:63500-67100, all of
# them `[reg+reg*4+disp]' into the same 0x44-byte record): the dword-width
# fields are at -68, -44, +0, +4, +14, +20 and +28, with +0 read as a dword six
# times and +14 nine times. Every one of the ten sites below is a 16-bit access
# landing INSIDE one of those dwords, and every constant involved (0x19, 0x38,
# 0x39, 0x3f, 0x47) is a plausible exponent and an implausible mantissa.
# All ten take delta -2: the high half of a big-endian dword sits at the dword's
# own address.

FUNC_000878: add word [esi+eax*4+0x10],byte +0x19 -- +25 to the exponent of the dword at +0xe

FUNC_000882: add word [ebx+edi*4+0x2],byte +0x3f -- +63 to the exponent of the dword at +0

FUNC_000884: mov word [esi+eax*4+0x2],0x47 -- the exponent of the dword at +0, clamped
